security_audit.summary: Most external command findings are markdown code fences or inline examples. The verification script only checks local skill text. The audit confirmed low-risk use of live Strimzi URLs and added one high-severity semantic issue for plaintext external Kafka access.

remediation.suggestion: Pin Strimzi installer and example URLs to a reviewed version, and tell users to inspect manifests before applying them to a cluster.
Change the production example to require TLS and authentication for any external Kafka listener, or mark plaintext listeners as development-only.

The quick start applies a live Strimzi install manifest from strimzi.io to a Kubernetes cluster. This is expected for Strimzi setup, but an unpinned remote manifest can change over time.
The quick start applies a remote Kafka example manifest from strimzi.io to the cluster. This is legitimate guidance, but fetching latest remote YAML creates supply-chain and drift risk.
The standard install repeats use of the live Strimzi installer URL. The source is expected, but the unpinned latest endpoint can change without review.
The namespace-scoped install downloads the Strimzi manifest with curl from a remote URL. This is normal documentation, but users should pin and review the downloaded manifest.
The cleanup command references the live Strimzi installer URL to delete resources. It is legitimate cleanup guidance, but relying on latest remote YAML can produce unexpected deletion behavior.

content.user_title: Deploy Kafka on Kubernetes with Strimzi
content.value_statement: Kafka on Kubernetes requires careful operator setup, storage choices, and service discovery. This skill gives clear Strimzi steps for deployment, topics, testing, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Guides Strimzi operator installation in a Kubernetes namespace.
Provides single-node and three-node Kafka cluster examples using KRaft mode.
Shows KafkaTopic creation and topic inspection workflows.
Explains console producer and consumer testing through Strimzi Kafka images.
Covers service discovery, Prometheus metrics setup, troubleshooting, and cleanup.
Includes a Dapr pub/sub component example for Kafka integration.
limitations: Does not configure managed Kafka services such as Confluent Cloud or Amazon MSK.
Requires an existing Kubernetes cluster and kubectl access.
Examples need security review before production use.
Does not automate backups, upgrades, or disaster recovery planning.

use_cases.title: Create a Development Kafka Cluster
use_cases.description: Set up a single-node Strimzi Kafka cluster for local or shared development testing.

use_cases.title: Plan a Production Strimzi Deployment
use_cases.description: Review replicas, persistent storage, resource limits, listeners, and operator installation choices.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Kafka on Kubernetes
use_cases.description: Inspect Kafka resources, pods, logs, events, bootstrap services, and common readiness problems.

prompt_templates.title: Install Strimzi and Kafka
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup on an existing Kubernetes cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to guide a development Kafka deployment on Kubernetes. Include namespace creation, Strimzi installation, cluster creation, and readiness checks.

prompt_templates.title: Create Topics and Test Clients
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a Kafka topic and test it with console producer and consumer clients. Explain each verification step.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Production Kafka
prompt_templates.scenario: Adapt the example for a durable cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a three-node Strimzi Kafka cluster. Include storage, resource requests, replication settings, listeners, and security review notes.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Cluster Failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced troubleshooting for operators and brokers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to troubleshoot a Kafka cluster that is not ready. Check operator status, Kafka resources, pods, logs, events, storage, and bootstrap services.

output_examples.input: I need a development Kafka cluster on Kubernetes.
output_examples.output: A concise setup plan with namespace creation, Strimzi operator installation, single-node Kafka deployment, readiness checks, and basic cleanup guidance.

output_examples.input: My Kafka pods are not becoming ready.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist covering Kafka resource status, pod descriptions, logs, events, storage class problems, and memory limits.

output_examples.input: I want Kafka for a Dapr pub/sub component.
output_examples.output: A Kafka bootstrap service summary and Dapr integration guidance that identifies broker address, namespace, and authentication assumptions.

best_practices: Pin Strimzi versions and review Kubernetes manifests before applying them.
Use TLS, authentication, and network controls for non-local Kafka listeners.
Test commands in a non-production namespace before changing shared clusters.
anti_patterns: Applying latest remote manifests directly to production clusters.
Using plaintext external Kafka listeners for sensitive workloads.
Deleting persistent volume claims before backup and retention review.

faq.question: What does this skill deploy?
faq.answer: It guides Apache Kafka deployment on Kubernetes using the Strimzi operator and KRaft mode examples.

faq.question: Does it support managed Kafka services?
faq.answer: No. It is intended for Kubernetes-based Kafka clusters, not Confluent Cloud, Amazon MSK, or other managed services.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: You need kubectl access to a Kubernetes cluster and permission to install Strimzi resources.

faq.question: Can it create Kafka topics?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows KafkaTopic CRD creation and commands for listing and describing topics.

faq.question: Is the production example ready to copy?
faq.answer: No. Review storage, networking, TLS, authentication, resource limits, and backup requirements before production use.

faq.question: Does it include Dapr guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a Dapr pub/sub component example that points to a Strimzi Kafka bootstrap service.
